correctness.rationale: For each fixed count t, sums of pk+1, pk+2, pk+3 fill [t(pk+1),t(pk+3)] exactly, so the quotient membership intervals have integer endpoints kt+ceil(t/p) and kt+floor(3t/p). The first is t0=ceil(p/3). The gaps between successive nonempty intervals have exact positive length max(0,k-2q-floor(3r/p)), with t=pq+r; these lengths are nonincreasing in t and exhaust maximal blocks. Residue counts j=0,1,2 and the q=0 boundary give c_p for odd k-ell and p-c_p for even k-ell, plus the initial length kt0. Summing frequencies proves both corollaries. The standalone checker recomputed 219 cases, 6,989 gap blocks, 40,685 missing integers across 2,708,025 independently constructed membership positions. Finite tests are corroboration, not the proof.

value.rationale: The result closes a natural two-parameter three-denomination quotient interval problem with the complete distribution of maximal missing block lengths. Unlike genus and Frobenius, it distinguishes the density of every short length; its parity alternation and sharp p=4 missing-length transition are meaningful structural information. The p=2 previously covered case is expressly excluded, and the p>=3 theorem is not a routine fixed-parameter table.
